title: Maximum Value of Concatenated Binary Segments
summary: Given two arrays, nums1 and nums0, each of size n, where nums1[i] is the count of '1's and nums0[i] is the count of '0's in the i-th segment, construct segments of '1's followed by '0's.
statement: Given two arrays, nums1 and nums0, each of size n, where nums1[i] is the count of '1's and nums0[i] is the count of '0's in the i-th segment, construct segments of '1's followed by '0's. Rearrange these segments to form a binary string. Return the maximum possible integer value of this string modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: nums1 and nums0 have equal positive length and nonnegative counts; each segment is 1 repeated nums1[i] then 0 repeated nums0[i].
Rearrange whole segments to maximize the concatenated binary integer.
hints: For two segments A and B, place A first exactly when concatenation AB is lexicographically at least BA.
For runs 1^a0^b this comparison reduces to: all-one segments first, mixed segments by more ones then fewer zeros, and all-zero segments last.
Stream the ordered bits modulo the prime, using a power of two to append zero runs efficiently.
The pairwise exchange rule is transitive under this key, so removing every inverted adjacent pair reaches a globally maximal concatenation.
